result.evidence: Continuous-mass finite-volume particle calculation with inherited geometry, drag, sticking, chipping and liquid-saturated growth. Collision events are exact at fixed layer properties; volume, vertical mixing, split-time, fractional-fragment allocation and sampling errors remain distinct. No observed-storm calibration or giant-aggregate survival law.
result.reading_rule: The final null diameter means +infinity and retains all arrivals. Moment arrays are unnormalized cumulative extensive quantities per square metre. Quantiles are per realization. Fractional fragments retain water and number in local allocation remainders, participate after allocation of a whole particle, and are bounded separately; no fragment water is discarded. The demand bound excludes delayed-allocation feedback. Physical tail predictions require convergence and suitable geometry, fracture and cloud exposure.

acceptance.criterion: All cases complete; relative water/number residuals below 1e-10; every listed refinement changes mean mass CDF by at most 0.05 and mean flux/d50/d90/d99 by at most 5%. These practical numerical screens do not bound sampling uncertainty or establish physical validity.

evidence: Complete finite-volume prescribed-cloud calculations with explicit refinement and realization uncertainty. No physical size cap, giant-aggregate fracture, evolving geometry, or climate-resolved moist trajectories.
reading_rule: Whole realizations supply standard errors. Correlated particles within a column are not independent uncertainty samples. Mean quantiles are means of realization quantiles, not pooled-population quantiles. Source flux and duration agree in expectation with the frozen column. Upwind settling matches its height-space generator; continuous masses remove pivot allocation. Mass conservation does not imply volume convergence. Failed refinements prevent use as snowfall or optical predictions.
